To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have proposed and analyzed a new distributed SNR estimation algorithm for sensor networks that is robust against noise and has a constant-modulus transmit scheme that is optimal in the asymptotic regime and that we have shown that the proposed algorithm outperforms other distributed SNR estimation schemes.

(i) the joint estimator decouples, (ii) the joint asymptotic variance is equal to the asymptotic variance of the mean plus the asymptotic variance the variance estimator, and (iii) the asymptotic variance depends on the transmit power constraint and sensing noise distribution.

the asymptotic variance of the SNR estimators is minimized by a per-sensor transmit power constraint, that the asymptotic relative efficiency is maximized by a total transmit power constraint, and that the asymptotic efficiency is maximized for Gaussian sensing noise.
In summary, our research is concerned with
distributed estimation of signal to noise ratio over multiple access channel.
the design of a robust and distributed SNR estimator that is applicable to a wide class of sensing noise distributions and is amenable to implementation.
the design of a sensor network to provide a distributed estimate of SNR, using a single time snapshot.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the SNR estimators are robust against noise distribution and the phase-modulation scheme ensures a fixed total power constraint.
the proposed SNR estimators are asymptotic relative efficiency optimal, and that the constant-modulus phase transmission scheme is optimal in the asymptotic relative efficiency sense.

for the case of a total transmit power constraint, the SNR estimator performs well for both Gaussian and Cauchyan sensing noise, and that for the case where each sensor has its own power constraint, the estimator performs better for Gaussian sensing noise than for Cauchyan sensing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in a sensor network, the fusion center can estimate the mean and variance of the signal embedded in the noise, using the phase-modulated observations from the sensors.
we have developed distributed estimators that require a single time snapshot and a single transmission from each sensor to the fusion center, and yet achieve asymptotic minimum-variance estimation.
the proposed SNR estimators are asymptotic efficient only in the case of Gaussian sensing noise distribution and are robust across a wide range of noise distribution.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a single transmission of a constant-modulus phase-modulated signal over a multiple-access channel can be used to jointly estimate both the mean and the SNR, which is useful for distributed signal detection and estimation applications.
the proposed distributed SNR estimation technique is optimal when the noise is Gaussian, and is robust to the noise distribution when the total transmit power is constrained.

a single set of transmission parameters, which are optimal for the Gaussian case, can be used for the SNR estimation of a signal embedded in Gaussian and Cauchyanoise, with the same asymptotic performance as the optimal transmission parameters.
